svg.title: Each team reaches only its own data and models; data science also reads a remote source
svg.desc: One shared Azure Databricks workspace sliced by Entra ID group, with Foundry via Unity Gateway and a cross-subscription source

text.tspan: Each team reaches only its own data and models; data science also reads a remote source
One shared Azure Databricks workspace sliced by Entra ID group, with Foundry via Unity Gateway and a cross-subscription source
Shared account, one container per slice
The team’s Entra ID group holds EXECUTE on its model provider service, a Unity Catalog object in the team’s own catalog.

Calls go through Unity Gateway to the team’s Foundry, authenticated by the slice’s service credential, whose managed identity holds Azure AI User on that Foundry. Engineering and analytics share one Foundry; data science has its own.
The group holds USE CATALOG on its catalog only; the catalog’s managed location is reached through the slice’s storage credential.
Both credentials reference the slice’s access connector for Azure Databricks, which uses the slice’s user-assigned managed identity.
That identity holds Storage Blob Data Contributor on the slice’s container only.
The group has READ on its secret scope, backed by the slice’s Key Vault (Key Vault Secrets User for the AzureDatabricks application). Every slice repeats steps 1–6 with its own resources.
Data science only: the group holds READ FILES (no WRITE FILES) on an external location for the remote sales-raw path.
The external location uses the slice’s storage credential; its managed identity holds Storage Blob Data Reader on the remote container (cross-subscription RBAC, same Entra tenant).

Reads travel over a private endpoint (dfs) in the workspace VNet, approved by the remote account owner, with a privatelink.dfs DNS zone. For serverless compute, the same link is an NCC private endpoint rule.
